PoolCard's fmt sentinel masks the symptom — user sees '—' for ALL trades when only one was malformed.
impacts: Single bad fill corrupts whole-day volume. Silent: '—' looks identical to 'no trades'. Now reachable via the live data layer (no longer behind the iter-1 stub).

title: manifest.ts re-exports types from types.ts; two canonical paths
recommendations: Drop the re-export from manifest.ts. Update App.tsx (line 14) and dataLayer.ts (line 19) to `import type { ... } from './types.js'` directly. One canonical home for the types, every consumer imports from it.
descriptions: manifest.ts on lines 22-23 does both `export type { PoolDescriptor, LoadedManifest } from './types.js';` and `import type { LoadedManifest, PoolDescriptor } from './types.js';`. The re-export exists to support consumers that import these types from manifest.ts (e.g. App.tsx line 14, dataLayer.ts line 19). Now that types.ts is the documented source of truth, the re-export adds a second canonical path for the same types without any value — the consolidator can no longer tell which file is canonical for these types just by reading imports.
impacts: Doubles the surface area for type drift: a future change that adds a field to LoadedManifest in types.ts will silently propagate, but a future change that wraps LoadedManifest in manifest.ts (e.g. branding) will diverge from types.ts. Also confuses future readers about whether manifest.ts owns these types or just consumes them.
evidence:
export type { PoolDescriptor, LoadedManifest } from './types.js';
import type { LoadedManifest, PoolDescriptor } from './types.js';

title: T-022 sentinel-marker test still satisfied by any literal mention of chain-shape.md
recommendations: Same as iter-1: rename the test as a sentinel-marker check or strengthen by parsing chain-shape.md for backtick-quoted field names and requiring at least one cross-reference.
descriptions: Iter-1 R5-005 unchanged. T-022 walks src/ and matches `/chain-shape\.md/i` against any file content — a doc comment alone satisfies it. types.ts now contains 'derived empirically from the capture in independent/01-market-stats/notes/chain-shape.md', which is a comment and not a derivation proof. If a developer later edits a field name to disagree with the captured shape but leaves the comment, the test still passes.

title: T-013 second sub-test still does not pin in-window result count (vacuous predicate hole)
recommendations: Tests are sealed. File as low-priority strengthening.
Tests are sealed.
descriptions: Iter-1 R5-006 unchanged. The third sub-test asserts `expect(result.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(50)`. The sibling `responder).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` already locks pagination behavior. The looseness is purely on result-length specificity.

Note iter-2's H-1 fix added a `poolId !== poolId` filter that early-skips events; this filter could (in a hypothetical future bug) silently drop everything and the test wouldn't catch it because all six in-window events in the fixture happen to have `poolId === POOL_ID`.

An aggressive early-bail or over-aggressive filter would pass.

recommendations: Tests are sealed.

title: Vite middleware is appropriately small — confirms no over-engineering of CR-3
recommendations: No action. Optionally: read MANIFEST_DISK_PATH from an env var fallback if the sandbox is ever moved out of ~/workspace/, but contract pins the path so this is not needed.

No over-abstraction (no plugin wrapper, no factory, no env-driven path). This is the right scope for a dev-only manifest passthrough.

title: PoolCard fmt() uses String(value) — fine numerics render as scientific notation
recommendations: Mirror sparkline's toFixed approach: `value.toLocaleString(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 6 })` or pin per-field toFixed.
descriptions: Iter-1 R3-017 NOT FIXED. fmt() returns `String(value)` for finite numbers; very small or very large values render as scientific notation (e.g. '1.23e-8') which a non-technical user might misread as the sentinel. Now reachable: iter-1 the data layer was stubbed to zeros so this was hidden; iter-2 wires real chain values where small mid-prices and depth-per-tick values are plausible.
impacts: Cosmetic / latent UX bug. Not load-bearing for any AC.
